A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DCIS and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A. All 12 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2 support comparison, including matching material that was relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original DCIS experiments measuring perplexity, passkey retrieval, LongBench performance, and Open LLM Leaderboard scores, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Llama3 evaluation, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and experiments using LongPPL as the search objective.

M1.justification: Section 6.5 introduces a tested variant replacing the PPL search objective with LongPPL. The main divide-and-conquer algorithm, YaRN initialization, update strategy, and adaptive scaling factors remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The reported coverage remains Proof-pile, PG19, passkey retrieval, LongBench, and Open LLM Leaderboard tasks. Llama3 adds a model configuration; the additional sensitivity and objective experiments do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds PI to the main perplexity comparison. CodeLlama was already evaluated in v1 Figure 1 and is retained through tabulation in v2; the other established comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama3-8B evaluation and controlled Llama2-7B experiments on 16k sequences varying the search range, increment count, and optimization metric. The existing fine-tuning budgets, learning rate, ten-sample perplexity evaluation, and 50 passkey tests per length are retained.

E4.justification: New Sections 6.4 and 6.5 substantially expand the diagnostic analyses: Tables 3–4 test sensitivity to search range and increment count, while Table 5 tests substituting LongPPL for PPL. The earlier ASF ablation and appendix studies of fine-tuning steps and shorter contexts remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds PI and DCIS-4k perplexity entries in Table 1, Llama3 results in Figure 4c, and sensitivity and objective results in Tables 3–5. Examples include PI's 64k PPL of 187.65 and LongPPL decreasing from 12.99 to 2.64 after search. The LongBench and appendix score tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The mathematical operations in Equations 1–8 and the search-space calculation are retained; edits clarify indexing and sorted-value notation. Section 6.4 adds qualitative reasoning about sensitivity, without a new formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the stated analytical contribution to include hyperparameter sensitivity and framework scalability. The central claims about short-to-long generalization, reduced fine-tuning costs, effectiveness without fine-tuning, and approximately doubled search efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning near-optimal search regions, parameter stability, and flexibility across optimization metrics. It removes the RoPE-decay explanation and the explicit warning that search cannot guarantee optimal scaling factors, while retaining the Phi-3 failure case and associated applicability limitation.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly documents fine-tuning token budgets, and Sections 6.4–6.5 specify settings for the added experiments. These disclosures do not establish changes to existing training procedures. A new inconsistency remains: Section 6.4 states [5,5], whereas Table 4 specifies [-5,5].

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Llama3, CodeLlama, LongPPL, and several background works, and removes Barbero et al. alongside the RoPE-decay discussion. The main positioning against scaling, compression, and sparse-attention approaches is retained; many other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 revises and shortens parts of the introduction, rewrites the conclusion, adds two analysis subsections and acknowledgments, and updates authors and affiliations. The principal section order and most method and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redesigned to show model integration and the branching search. Other plots are reformatted, Figure 4 gains a Llama3 panel, and four tables are added. Existing tables and figures are also relocated or renumbered, with the appendix displays largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The added Llama3 evaluation, sensitivity tests, explicit perplexity and training-budget table, and redesigned method diagram improve validation and clarity. The gains are limited: Table 5 reports different metrics rather than a common-metric comparison of objectives, and v2 removes the useful optimality caveat. Overall, the additions provide a modest improvement while retaining the established results.
